title: Rast wins the Hockenheim finale, Paffett takes the 2018 title
dek: René Rast won the last DTM race of 2018 by 3.786 seconds for Audi, but third place for Gary Paffett was enough to give Mercedes the drivers’ title by four points.

chapters.title: Four points of margin on Saturday night
text: Saturday had reshaped the title fight. Rast won Race 1 for his fifth victory in a row, Paffett finished fourth and Paul di Resta, who arrived at Hockenheim as championship leader, was only eighth. Paffett went back to the top, six points ahead of di Resta and 15 clear of Rast, with the final race of the DTM’s 2018 season, and Mercedes’ last in the series, still to come.
All three of them could still take the title on Sunday, and Paffett, with a new qualifying session to come, held the advantage.

chapters.title: Wittmann snatches pole from Rast
text: Marco Wittmann was the story of Sunday morning. Having missed qualifying on Saturday after his practice crash, he took pole for the finale with a 1m32.683s in the final minute, 0.054s faster than Rast, who had led much of the session. It was Wittmann’s first pole of the season, a result that rewarded the RMG crew for the work they had put into repairing the #11 car.

Paffett, only fourth during the mid-session lull, jumped to third on his last lap with a 1m32.846s, which, with the point for third, lifted his advantage over di Resta to seven and left Rast 14 behind him. Rast needed a podium finish to keep any hope alive, and a win would still have required Paffett to finish outside the top four.

Behind the top three came Spengler’s BMW in fourth, Farfus fifth and Mortara sixth, the only other Mercedes in the top ten. Eriksson, Eng, Müller and Glock followed. Di Resta had a quiet session and lined up 11th, with a lot of work to do. The Audi of Frijns, which would be the quickest car at the end of the race, was last on the grid in 18th.

chapters.title: Rast wins the start
text: Rast got a perfect launch and slipped to the inside of Wittmann into the first corner, while Wittmann got away slowly and could not hit back. Paffett stayed third, and over the first stint the leading trio ran in line, with Wittmann in the DRS window and glancing at Rast’s mirrors for several laps before dropping back.

Di Resta jumped from 11th to eighth on the opening lap, but had to hand a place back to Eng and slipped to tenth. Needing a gamble, he was the first driver into the pits within the first seven laps. Mortara got past Spengler for fourth.

chapters.title: The undercut that mattered
text: Paffett was the first of the leaders to stop, with Rast following soon afterwards. Rast’s Audi crew changed his tyres in 6.8s against 7.6s for Paffett, and Rast rejoined with a lead of more than four seconds. Wittmann stayed out longer, and when he finally came in, Paffett’s earlier stop had undercut him and put the Mercedes ahead on the virtual order.

The drivers yet to stop made the running awkward. Rast had to deal with Juncadella and Wehrlein on the road, while Jamie Green in the second Rosberg Audi held up Paffett until Wittmann came within DRS distance and passed him on lap 22.

chapters.title: Müller and Frijns come for Paffett
text: While the top three ran out the race, the real threat to the title came from behind. Müller and Frijns had both delayed their stops until deep into the second half, and on fresh tyres they scythed through a field of BMWs and fading Mercedes. Müller was fourth with just over three laps to go, and Frijns, who set the fastest lap of the race on lap 27, passed Spengler for fifth on the penultimate lap.
Paffett, who was managing tyre wear and keeping an eye on his mirrors, had just enough in hand. He later said he had seen the Audis appear five laps from the end but knew they would not catch him.

chapters.title: A champion in third
text: Rast crossed the line 3.786s ahead of Wittmann, his sixth consecutive win and the seventh of his season, with Paffett another 12.052s behind. Paffett had held off Müller by 1.4s, and Frijns finished a further 1.7s back in fifth. Bruno Spengler led home a BMW quintet in sixth, followed by Farfus, Eng, Eriksson and Glock.

Mercedes struggled for race pace in the finale: Paffett was the only one of its drivers to run competitively, while Mercedes cars filled five of the last six places. Di Resta finished 14th, ending any chance of the title.

chapters.title: Mercedes leaves with the triple
text: Paffett’s third place gave him 255 points to Rast’s 251 and di Resta’s 233, the narrowest of margins and his second DTM title, 13 years after the first in 2005. Mercedes also won the manufacturers’ and teams’ titles, completing a triple in its final year after 30 seasons in the series. Paffett called it the best day of his life and said he had spent 13 years working to get back to the top. In the closing laps, he admitted, he had begun counting down the laps left in his DTM career and almost slid off the road because his concentration drifted. He also thanked everyone at Mercedes for the 15 years he had spent with the marque in the series.

Rast’s run of six wins came too late by four points. He said he was a little disappointed and admitted that thoughts of what might have been would come, though they counted for nothing in racing, before thanking the many people behind his streak of six wins in a row and saying he already looked forward to next year. Wittmann, who rebounded from a wrecked Saturday with pole position and second place, said Rast had simply been a little too quick on the day, and it was a good way for him to finish the season on the podium. Audi’s Dieter Gass said the team was proud to have come from nowhere at the start of the season to finish the year with six straight wins.

Di Resta’s weekend added just four points to the 229 he had arrived with, and he slipped from first to third in the standings. He said it was simply not his weekend, congratulated Paffett and noted that the team goal, a Mercedes champion, had been achieved. Mercedes team principal Ulrich Fritz said the unbelievable fight had ended in the closest possible way, and thanked Audi and BMW for the years of racing together.

Paffett’s DTM career ended with the title, as he moves to Formula E with HWA. The grid will still have three manufacturers in 2019, with Aston Martin entering through R-Motorsport as a third marque and HWA, Mercedes’ long-time DTM team, running the programme.

facts.v: Paffett finished the season on 255 points, four clear of Rast (251) and 22 ahead of di Resta (233).
